acceptance: Reproduce the live 2026-08-02 cadence evidence: nominal short polling produces roughly 51 to 80 second cycles and delayed queue-to-start because serial cycle work is followed by another full sleep.

Schedule from a monotonic deadline: subtract elapsed cycle work from the target interval, do not add a full interval after slow work, and define deterministic overrun/catch-up behavior that cannot busy-loop.
Keep provider/network, git/GitHub, evidence rendering, and other slow I/O outside runtime-admission, canonical task-state, and activity locks; document and test the global lock order.

Batch logically related runtime and canonical mutations per phase and reuse one authoritative snapshot where safe instead of reloading and journaling per task; preserve fail-closed CAS and audit ordering.
Expose bounded per-phase elapsed time, lock-hold time, cycle elapsed time, cadence overshoot, queue-to-start latency, and batch counts without logging credentials or unbounded task data.

Regression tests use a fake monotonic clock and injected slow phases to prove fixed cadence, overrun behavior, no busy loop, bounded lock holds, batch atomicity, crash recovery, and unchanged dispatch decisions.

Preserve dependency, priority, worker limits, failure-loop/chair triage, task-scoped quota/auth fallback, exact-head review, active leases, explicit Human/Ops reviewer, and existing rollback semantics.
Codex and Codex2 remain separate configured account and quota groups. Do not hardcode account equivalence and do not add a global mutual-review ban.

Use a clean task worktree from current origin/dev, commit only declared scope, run focused and full supervisor plus ai-status regressions, py_compile, JSON, diff and trailer checks, open PR to dev, obtain exact-head Human/Ops review, merge and canonical archive.
No live service restart or deployment belongs to this source task. Rollback is merge revert; live promotion is the dependent governed V8 canary.

Evidence: docs/deployment/evidence/supervisor/SUP-SCHEDULER-FIXED-CADENCE-BATCH-MUTATIONS-OPERATOR-V9-20260802/evidence.json. Exact-head validation: supervisor 561/561, ai-status 165/165, py_compile, JSON, git diff --check, and trailer gate passed. Please perform Human/Ops exact-head review.

Human/Ops rejected PR #4520 exact head 015d02d32239d03ebdf77b7fc888164ff893a775. Blocking crash/cleanup/telemetry findings: (1) reserved process_queue suppresses the immediate post-launch save, but the reservation persists no launch intent or receipt. Deterministic hard-crash injection after external process launch and before CAS produced supervisor exit 77 with launched_process_alive=true, runtime_worker_persisted=false, reservation_remains=true, so a live worker can be orphaned and the task/event can be redispatched. Restore durable pre/post-launch recovery/adoption or equivalent and test process death at this exact boundary. (2) _run_with_deferred_dispatch_status_syncs moved termination confirmation outside finally; if the locked operation raises after scheduling termination, the function exits before _flush_deferred_runtime_side_effects. Injection recorded one scheduled termination and zero flush calls. Cleanup that must run on exception cannot be dropped; add regression coverage. (3) reserve_started, commit_started, and lock_started are sampled before blocking acquisition, so runtime_lock_hold_seconds includes wait time rather than actual exclusive hold. Measure true hold separately so the canary's bounded-lock evidence is truthful. Preserve separate Codex/Codex2 configured account/quota groups and do not add a global mutual-review ban. Re-run full exact-head tests/evidence and re-handoff.

PR #4520 repaired head ab0d79e33bb1dfff452c93c32a96721168222ad9 is ready for exact-head re-review. Evidence: docs/deployment/evidence/supervisor/SUP-SCHEDULER-FIXED-CADENCE-BATCH-MUTATIONS-OPERATOR-V9-20260802/evidence.json. It covers hard exit 77 launch-intent adoption, post-launch receipt adoption, exception-safe deferred cleanup, and acquisition-excluding lock-hold telemetry. Full supervisor 565 tests + 158 subtests and ai-status 165 tests + 31 subtests pass.

Exact-head ab0d79e33 rejected. Three blocking gaps remain: (1) a durable launch_intent with no receipt and no unique marker is retained forever, so adapter failure before launch can permanently freeze process_queue and prevent quota/auth fallback or reassignment; add bounded, process-proven stale-intent resolution plus no-launch/ambiguous-marker regressions; (2) claim_next_task_for_agent still wraps load_provider_report, process_queue/worktree+adapter launch, and dashboard refresh in _run_with_deferred_dispatch_status_syncs exclusive runtime admission, violating the slow-I/O-outside-lock acceptance and preserving the self-claim latency path; refactor to short reservation/CAS phases and prove actual entry-point lock depth; (3) _run_with_deferred_dispatch_status_syncs flushes canonical status, archive, and activity side effects after an operation exception, even though its runtime mutation did not complete; on failure only exact termination cleanup may run unless committed state is proven, with an injected regression. Preserve distinct Codex/Codex2 account/quota groups and no global mutual-review ban.

PR #4520 exact head fb923abe2182acb4b5c10a0e557040b968598008 is ready for independent re-review. Latest rejected-head blockers are covered by bounded exact-process stale-intent recovery, reservation/CAS self-claim with named slow paths at lock depth zero, and failure-path discard of uncommitted canonical/archive/activity effects while preserving exact termination cleanup. Evidence: docs/deployment/evidence/supervisor/SUP-SCHEDULER-FIXED-CADENCE-BATCH-MUTATIONS-OPERATOR-V9-20260802/evidence.json. Verified supervisor 570 tests + 158 subtests; ai-status 165 tests + 31 subtests; py_compile, JSON, diff, and trailer gates.

Exact-head fb923abe rejected: launch recovery lacks post-intent generation binding. Independent fake-/proc reproduction proves both a worker_runner candidate whose generation necessarily predates a future prepared_epoch_seconds and a marker started in 2020 with a freshly updated heartbeat mtime are accepted as run-old. _runtime_launch_process_candidates never compares process start epoch to the intent, and _runtime_launch_marker_candidates filters mtime rather than marker started_at; recovery can therefore adopt an older same-task/agent run and bind it to the new queue_event_id. Add end-to-end temporal proof (PID start epoch from btime+ticks or exact launch token), prevent unique-marker fallback from bypassing it, and add negative pre-intent process plus fresh-heartbeat-marker tests while retaining post-intent adoption and distinct Codex/Codex2 groups.

PR #4520 exact head ba3b176500f557944eb6f3e08709361281609989 is ready for independent re-review. Temporal recovery now rejects pre-intent /proc generations via btime+start ticks/CLK_TCK plus a persisted boot-tick boundary; marker selection uses immutable started_at so fresh heartbeat mtime cannot bypass unique-marker fallback; Codex/Codex2 remain distinct. Evidence: docs/deployment/evidence/supervisor/SUP-SCHEDULER-FIXED-CADENCE-BATCH-MUTATIONS-OPERATOR-V9-20260802/evidence.json. Verified supervisor 573 + 158 subtests, ai-status 165 + 31 subtests, py_compile, JSON, full-range diff and trailers.

Exact-head ba3b1765 rejected: the unique running-marker fallback still bypasses the new exact boot-tick process proof within the same wall-clock second. Independent reproduction sets intent prepared_epoch=18:00:00.900 with prepared_boottime_ticks, an older running marker started_at=18:00:00, and a fresh heartbeat; _runtime_launch_marker_candidates accepts run-old-same-second because it floors prepared_epoch, and recovery adopts it whenever the exact /proc scan correctly returns zero pre-intent candidates. Require any running/live marker to match a post-intent process candidate that passed pid_start_ticks >= prepared_boottime_ticks; marker-only adoption may be limited to terminal/dead evidence, or use an exact token/tick in the marker. Add the same-second negative end-to-end test. Preserve the existing post-intent crash adoption and distinct Codex/Codex2 groups.

Exact-head review rejects c9299f51a4ccb6d76bd3964f060cfde87673201b for one remaining strict temporal boundary. In _runtime_launch_marker_candidates the check is marker_started_at.timestamp() < prepared_epoch, so equality is accepted. Both worker_runner utc_now() and supervisor _isoformat_utc() truncate microseconds; a legacy/reconstructed intent whose prepared epoch comes from second-resolution prepared_at can therefore accept a same-second running or terminal marker even though equality cannot prove post-intent order. Terminal/dead marker-only recovery then bypasses /proc. Change the exclusion to <= (strictly post-intent only), add exact-equality running and terminal negative tests while retaining the strictly-next-second terminal positive and exact-process hard-crash positive. Independent exact-head validation otherwise passed: 21 focused supervisor tests, 4 ai-status batch tests, JSON and diff checks; net scope is correct.
